summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of systolic heart failure (EF 20%), ischemic cardiomyopathy, type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and obesity, was readmitted for worsening shortness of breath and chest heaviness one week after a prior discharge. He reported increased fluid intake, weight gain, and persistent symptoms despite medication adherence. Evaluation revealed acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation with elevated BNP, pulmonary congestion on imaging, and volume overload. He was treated with IV diuresis, transitioned to oral torsemide, and maintained on amiodarone for recent non-sustained ventricular tachycardia. His symptoms improved, weight decreased to dry weight, and he was discharged home with service, follow-up plans for medication management, and financial counseling support.
